title: Whose is it? Kenen … tämä on?
summary: Kenen means “whose”. It is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”); learn kenen as a whole.
prerequisiteSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
objectives: Ask whose singular thing this is with Kenen … tämä on?
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Kenen means “whose”. It is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”); learn kenen as a whole.
Ask Kenen pallo tämä on? — “Whose ball is this?” Put kenen before the basic noun, followed by tämä on. Because kenen asks who the owner is, do not add a personal possessive ending to that noun.
An answer can use an earlier learned owner phrase, for example minun palloni (“my ball”). Review can combine the question with a complete answer.
keyPoints: Whose is it? Kenen … tämä on?
Practise one singular possessed thing with the supporting forms shown.

steps: Begin with kenen (“whose”), the learned owner-question form of kuka (“who”).
Place the basic noun pallo (“ball”) next; the question does not name a personal owner, so add no personal suffix.
Finish with tämä (“this”) + on (“is”): Kenen + thing + tämä on?
Keep kenen (“whose”) before the thing being asked about.
Use basic kirja (“book”), not kirjani or kirjansa; those endings would name an owner.
Keep tämä on (“this is”) after the noun in this taught question order.
Choose kenen (“whose”) to ask about the owner, rather than kuka (“who”) as a person.
Use basic kynä (“pen”); its front vowels do not call for a possessive suffix in this question.
End with tämä on (“this is”), preserving Kenen + thing + tämä on?

commonMistakes: Use kenen (“whose”) to ask about ownership, rather than kuka (“who”).
Keep the basic noun without a personal possessive ending: Kenen pallo tämä on?, rather than Kenen pallonsa tämä on?
Put the thing immediately after kenen in the requested order, followed by tämä on.

parts.formation: Kuka means “who”; its learned genitive form kenen asks whose thing it is.
Keep the noun in its basic singular form. Kenen is not a personal owner pronoun, so do not add a personal suffix.
On identifies the singular thing; the question begins with kenen rather than onko.
